HX-400 shell-and-tube heat exchanger

A removable-bundle exchanger for duties where the process side fouls and somebody has to get inside it twice a year. Built to ASME VIII Division 1 and PED, in materials from carbon steel to titanium.

What it is for

The HX-400 is the unit we reach for when the duty is dirty. Crude preheat trains, quench-water service, glycol regeneration, evaporator condensate — anywhere the fouling factor in the datasheet is a guess and the real answer arrives eighteen months later as a pressure drop.

Everything about the design assumes the bundle comes out. The channel end is bolted rather than welded, the extraction rail is part of the unit rather than an accessory, and the tube layout leaves lanes wide enough for a lance rather than for a catalogue illustration.

Configuration

ParameterRange
Surface area18 to 940 m²
Shell diameter203 to 1500 mm
Design pressureFull vacuum to 150 barg
Design temperature−46 to 450 °C
TEMA typesAES, AEU, BEM, BKU, NEN
Tube materialsCarbon steel, 304L/316L, duplex 2205, super duplex, titanium grade 2, Alloy 825
CodesASME VIII Div 1 (U stamp), PED 2014/68/EU, CRN on request

Ordering and lead time

  • Standard carbon-steel configurations: 14 to 18 weeks from drawing approval.
  • Duplex and titanium: 22 to 30 weeks, material-dependent.
  • Retube of an existing unit, ours or another manufacturer's: 6 to 9 weeks.
  • Emergency bundle replacement from stock sizes: 10 working days.

What ships with it

  1. Thermal and mechanical design report, stamped.
  2. Material test certificates to EN 10204 3.1, and 3.2 where the code requires it.
  3. Hydrotest and NDT records.
  4. An extraction and cleaning procedure written for the unit rather than for the range.
  5. A spares list with the three items that actually get consumed marked as such.

Related equipment

Where the duty is clean and the plot space is tight, the PL-200 plate exchanger is usually the better answer. Where the process side carries solids, look at the separator range first.

We specified the HX-400 for quench-water duty because it was the only removable-bundle unit in the tender where the extraction rail was in the base scope rather than a line item.
